title: Human middle and inner ear
credit: SPL Inner Ear Atlas (Bartling, Jakab, Kikinis), Open Anatomy Project, 3D Slicer License. Simplified for BioEZ.

parts.label: Tympanic membrane (eardrum)
parts.info: Thin membrane that vibrates with sound and passes the vibration to the malleus.

parts.label: Malleus (hammer)
parts.info: First ossicle; its handle is attached to the eardrum.

parts.label: Incus (anvil)
parts.info: Middle ossicle linking the malleus to the stapes.

parts.label: Stapes (stirrup)
parts.info: Smallest bone in the body; its footplate pushes on the oval window of the cochlea.

parts.label: Bony labyrinth (cochlea, vestibule, semicircular canals)
parts.info: Fluid-filled inner ear: the cochlea for hearing, the vestibule and semicircular canals for balance.

parts.label: Osseous spiral lamina
parts.info: Bony shelf spiralling inside the cochlea that supports the basilar membrane.

parts.label: Round window
parts.info: Membrane-covered opening that bulges to release pressure as the stapes moves.

parts.label: Tensor tympani muscle
parts.info: Pulls the malleus to stiffen the eardrum against loud sounds.

parts.label: Stapedius muscle
parts.info: Smallest skeletal muscle; damps stapes movement in the acoustic reflex.

parts.label: Cochlear nerve
parts.info: Carries hearing signals from the cochlea to the brainstem.

parts.label: Vestibular nerve
parts.info: Carries balance signals from the vestibule and semicircular canals.

parts.label: Facial nerve
parts.info: Runs through the temporal bone close to the middle ear; supplies the stapedius.

parts.label: Internal carotid artery
parts.info: Major artery to the brain, passing just in front of the middle ear.

parts.label: Internal jugular vein
parts.info: Main vein draining the head, below the middle ear.
